pages.name: Family Branches: Major and Minor Bloodlines

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, Chapter One ("A Familiar Conceit").

The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} clan is not solely composed of Kindred bearing the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} surname. Over a thousand years of Embracing, the clan has absorbed a number of other mortal families entire, each retaining its own name, business specialty, and degree of trust from the Venetian founders. This expands on the base clan's brief mention of the Pisanob, Milliners, Dunsirn, and della Passaglia (see the main Giovanni compendium entry).

The three major families (co-opted wholesale, with their own extensive mortal and Kindred membership):

  • The Dunsirn — Scottish banking cannibals brought into the fold in the early 1700s for their shipping interests and centuries of accumulated financial favors across the United Kingdom and Ireland. They serve as one of the clan's chief moneymakers, tithing in cash rather than souls, and show little interest in Necromancy. Lupines have inexplicably raided Dunsirn estates on at least two occasions.
  • The Pisanob — Aztec priest-necromancers (originally calling themselves pisanob, a Mayan term for “ghosts of the dead that walk the earth”) Embraced during Cortes' conquest of Tenochtitlan in the early 16th century, when Giovanni observers recognized kindred necromantic mastery threatened by the same sort of Underworld storm the Giovanni themselves survived two centuries prior. Led by the corpse-visaged Pochtli, whose true origin (Giovanni or surviving Cappadocian — see the Premascine entry in this compendium) remains disputed within the clan.
  • The Milliners — A Boston family brought into the fold in the mid-1950s after patriarch Francis Milliner, spurned for the presidency of the Columbia Trust Company in favor of Joseph P. Kennedy, spent decades quietly ruining the Kennedy family's fortunes and legacy in revenge, impressing Augustus with his capacity for grudge-holding. Instrumental in the modern-nights Giovanni takeover of Boston; like the Dunsirn, largely uninterested in Necromancy.

Minor families (smaller absorbed merchant lines, each with a distinct specialty):

  • della Passaglia — Absorbed in the 1400s, opening trade with the Orient (firearms for silk, tea, and opium). In recent decades they have become the clan's resident experts in Kindred-of-the-East thanatology, and made contact with the Cathayan Penangallan (the “Golden Courts”) during the Cambodian killing fields of the 1970s, trading Western Kindred lore for unusually free access to mass death and soul-harvesting.
  • Ghiberti — Acquired in the early 17th century for their role in the transatlantic triangle trade; their study of West African concepts of the four-part soul and spiritual reincarnation produced the Cenotaph Path, a unique branch of Necromancy focused on tracking and binding wraiths.
  • Putanesca — (“of the whore”) A Sicilian family of criminals and enforcers acquired in the 1660s out of the Sicilian Mafia; they handle the clan's dirty work (street-level drug distribution, muscle, vendetta) and have short, violent tempers.
  • Rosselini — A family independently proficient in Necromancy before encountering the Giovanni (likely from shared Roman roots), bound into fealty after Claudius Giovanni tore the souls from the bodies of a Rosselini coven that crossed him in Rome. Rosselini necromancers are notorious for using excessive, gratuitously cruel force to compel spirits, often turning the spiriti they abuse into spettri.

Families under consideration for future acquisition (as of the clanbook's writing): the St. John (English Masons), the Rothstein (Jewish-American Kabbalists tied to Las Vegas), the Li Weng (Chinese geomancers in San Francisco), the Koenig (German arms manufacturers and death cultists), and the Beryn (Flemish merchants operating out of Luxembourg with African ties). A sixth candidate family, the Hidalgo of Mexico, was reportedly wiped out by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} or the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls} before formal absorption.

Storyteller/LARP note: These branch names function as ready-made Background/Contact or Mentor flavor and as answers to "which part of the family are you from" for Giovanni characters who are not blood-Giovanni proper. A character built from the Dunsirn, Milliner, or Pisanob lines should be treated mechanically identical to a Giovanni (same Clan Disciplines and clan Advantage/Disadvantage), but may reasonably lack in-family reverence for Necromancy training (Dunsirn/Milliner) or carry other narrative baggage (Pisanob ties to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls} rumor mill).

pages.name: Single-Blooded Status and the Proxy Kiss

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, Introduction ("Kissing Cousins") and Chapter One ("A Familiar Conceit")/Chapter Two ("It Runs in the Family").

Single-blooded vs. double-blooded: Since the Renaissance-era decay of the family's mortal customs, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} have practiced deliberate inbreeding ("keeping the blood pure") to concentrate the bloodline. A mortal @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} born of two parents who are themselves both Giovanni by blood is termed single-blooded and enjoys a real, if informal, elevated status and preference for the Embrace over a double-blooded relation (descended from a Giovanni through only one parent, such as a Milliner/Pisanob/Dunsirn cousin, or a more distantly diluted line). Not all Giovanni are the product of incest, but single-blooded status is prized and openly discussed within the family.

Storyteller/LARP note: This is a pure family-status distinction, not a mechanical Trait modifier. Recommend using it as a roleplay hook/Background justification (e.g. a single-blooded character may justify a discount or priority claim on family-only resources, mentors, or Embrace candidacy in Storyteller-adjudicated scenes) rather than a hardcoded Trait bonus.

The Proxy Kiss: Most mortal Giovanni relations never receive the Embrace, but a smaller pool are groomed first through the Proxy Kiss — a brutal period of ghouldom (regular vitae feeding without the Embrace itself) used to test and season a candidate before a final decision on whether to Embrace them is made. Undergoing the Proxy Kiss marks a mortal as being seriously considered for the family's inner circle; the family's need for control over its own ghoul-childer (bound by bloodbond loyalty back to a specific domitor/sire) is treated as a matter of clan security, since an unbound ghoul or a ghoul bound to an outsider domitor is viewed as a dangerous liability (as dramatized when the Milliner scion Stewart is revealed to be blood-bound to someone outside the family, provoking a furious response from the clan elder Diego Giovanni).

Storyteller/LARP note (Proxy Kiss): Mechanically, a character on the Proxy Kiss is a standard ghoul per this system's existing ghoul/Blood Bond rules (see the core rules for ghoul creation and the Blood Bond Trait mechanics) — the term is simply the Giovanni family's in-house name for a family-sanctioned ghoul candidacy, generally administered by a specific sire-to-be rather than an arbitrary domitor. No new mechanics are introduced; this is flavor/naming for existing ghoul rules within a Giovanni family context.

The April 4th reunion: The clan holds an annual, invitation-only family reunion each April 4th, distinct from more casual gatherings like the family Christmas party. Invitation to the April 4th reunion is a mark of favor and proximity to the family's inner (Kindred-aware) circle; most mortal relations are never invited, and those who are tend to already suspect the family's true nature even if never told outright.

pages.name: Dis Pater, the Premascine, and the Painful Kiss

text.content:
Source: Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, Chapter One ("A Familiar Conceit").

Dis Pater: The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}'s mortal Jovian ancestors practiced ancestor worship, venerating a founder-spirit identified with the Roman god of the underworld, Dis Pater ("Father Wealth"). Unlike most wraiths the clan otherwise views as exploitable resources, Dis Pater is treated with genuine, ingrained reverence by the anziani (elders) and even by Augustus himself, for three reasons the clan cites internally: (1) Dis Pater is powerful enough within wraith society to have historically shielded the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni} from Underworld retaliation by invoking the Dictum Mortuum against would-be wraith attackers, and can as easily turn that power against Giovanni who show him disrespect; (2) disrespecting Dis Pater is taken as indirect disrespect of Augustus, who reveres him; and (3) among the eldest Giovanni, devotion to Dis Pater (folded into the family's idiosyncratic Catholicism as a de facto patron saint) is simply a habit carried over from their mortal lives.

Storyteller/LARP note (Dis Pater): Recommend treating Dis Pater as a unique, Storyteller-controlled wraith NPC/patron for chronicle purposes — a potential source of aid, omens, or complications for Giovanni characters in good standing (or a source of misfortune for those who show him disrespect), rather than as a Trait-purchasable Background. No dot cost or Trait conversion is specified in the source text.

The Premascine: Giovanni Kindred Embraced before Augustus formally split the clan away from the Cappadocians in 1444 are called Premascine ("before the bite"), including figures such as Claudius Giovanni and the self-interested Ambrogino Giovanni. Rumor holds that other Premascine who opposed Augustus' bid for clan independence went into hiding rather than face destruction: some allegedly lairing beneath the submerged ruins of Old Venice (reachable, it's whispered, by a flooded well inside the family's own Venice Mausoleum), and others surfacing as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.pwzvpEssMLxrFaOG]{Harbingers of Skulls} — an old, hostile, and reputedly @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}-adjacent cabal blamed for the deaths of Giovanni such as Martino della Passaglia's sire, and rumored (unconfirmed) to have wiped out the Hidalgo family before it could be absorbed into the clan.

Storyteller/LARP note (Premascine/Harbingers): Both groups are presented in-text as rumor and Storyteller-adjudicated mystery, not as a playable sub-faction with defined Traits. Recommend using them as antagonist/plot-hook material (a Harbinger of Skulls elder NPC, a Premascine haunting a Giovanni's ancestral haven) rather than granting player characters membership.

The Curse of Lamia (an alternate account of the Kiss disadvantage): The base Giovanni clan entry in this compendium already notes the family's Kiss inflicts pain rather than pleasure on those they feed from (a social Disadvantage). This chapter offers one in-clan legend for its origin: during the purge of the Cappadocians, Augustus diablerized a Cappadocian cult leader named Lamia, whose dying curse (or, in Japheth's rival account, a deliberate curse woven into the shared vitae used to Embrace Augustus and sealed in the artifact called the True Vessel) is blamed for afflicting the entire Giovanni bloodline with the agonizing bite. The clanbook presents this explicitly as one of several competing, unverifiable legends, not a confirmed fact.

Storyteller/LARP note (Curse of Lamia): This is flavor/lore for the Disadvantage the base Giovanni entry already documents (painful Kiss/social distrust) — it does not change or add to that Disadvantage's existing mechanical effect, and Storytellers should feel free to use, ignore, or contradict this legend as suits their chronicle.
